messages.subject: (G)LM distribution functions
parts:
[changed subject, moved to stan-dev]


On 6/21/13 1:08 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>> I also think we could productively add regression distributions, e.g.
>>
>> real logistic_regression_log(int y, vector beta, vector x)
>> =def=
>> bernoulli_log(y, inv_logit(x' * beta))
>>
>> real linear_regression_log(real y, vector beta, vector x, real sigma)
>> =def=
>> normal_log(y,x' * beta,sigma)
>>
>>
> So for these, do we want to directly return bernoulli_log(y,inv_logit(x' * beta)) and normal_log(y,x'*beta,sigma)?

The motiviation is to make the implementation more efficient.
So you need a new vari type (for reverse mode) and to calculate
the derivatives w.r.t. y, x', beta (and sigma in the
case of linear regression).

I also changed the type of y in the linear case to real. Now the issue
is that these should be vectorized so that y can be a vector in both
cases. But we haven't really worked out multivariate vectorizations,
so there's some work to do there on figuring out which signatures to use
and how to implement it. A very likely way for linear regression to be
called would be as this:

double linear_regression_log(const Eigen::Vector<double,Dynamic,1>& y,
const Eigen::Vector<var,Dynamic,1>& beta,
const Eigen::Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic>& x)
=def=


var sum = 0;
for (n in 1:size(y))
sum += normal_log(y[n],x[n] * beta,sigma)

If y is size N and beta is size K, then x is an (N x K) matrix
and x[n] is a K-vector.

But we'd want it to handle all of the double/var alternations as well
as forward mode fvar.

Other generalized linear models could be done the same way,
like
real poisson_regression_log(int y, vector beta, vector x)
=def=
poisson_log_log(y,x' * beta)
=def=
poisson_log(y, exp(x' * beta))

The ' is just transpose, but the implementation should be like dot product
so that x and beta can be any vector or array types, and y could also be
vectorized.

- Bob
